items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Named CTEs (valid_words, synset_counts, word_aggregates, top500) make the steps easy to follow. Indentation is consistent. The short SQL aliases (sc, t, w) are normal SQL style. There are no comments, but the task forbids them.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The top-synset lookup is copy-pasted into two correlated subqueries: `(SELECT sc.synsetid ... LIMIT 1)` and `(SELECT sc.sense_cnt ... LIMIT 1)`. A ROW_NUMBER CTE would avoid this. The ORDER BY list also appears twice, in top500 and in the final SELECT.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: synset_counts selects `syn.domainid, syn.posid` without aggregating them, while grouping only by `s.wordid, s.synsetid`. This works only because SQLite accepts bare columns, and it is correct only if synsetid is unique in synsets. Nothing in the schema enforces that.

items.name: Semantically equivalent, not just equal on this data
items.name_zh: 语义等价而非仅在当前数据上相等
items.evidence: Thresholds, top-synset tie-break and final ordering are kept. But the query assumes synsets.synsetid and words.wordid are unique (no PK or index). It joins words after the LIMIT and counts top-synset senses on the synsets join, which the original does not. Same results on real data.
